claims.claim: the yellow perch models mis-estimated resting metabolism in a laboratory test, with growth errors tracking feeding rate (Bajer, Whitledge, Hayward & Zweifel 2003, abstract)
claims.note: Article not read. The Crossref abstract says it in substance: 'Results indicated deficiencies in estimates of resting routine metabolism by both models' and the growth-rate errors 'were strongly correlated with food consumption rate'. Its conditions, from the abstract: two size classes of age-2 yellow perch, each on two feeding schedules, at 21 °C; the two models were the Wisconsin (WI) and the Karas–Thoresson (KT) models. The abstract attributes the consumption-dependent errors to the costs of specific dynamic action, feeding activity metabolism or egestion and excretion, and the differences BETWEEN the models mainly to egestion and excretion. 'The yellow perch models' in the paper should read 'two yellow perch bioenergetics models (Wisconsin and Karas–Thoresson)', and the test was at one temperature (21 °C).
